TEST 1. WIND ENERGY FACILITIES (PORTUGAL)

Evelyn Cruz

2026-08-27

1. Introduction

This analysis investigates the spatial distribution of wind energy facilities in mainland Portugal, focusing on installed capacity, elevation, temporal growth, and intersections with Natura 2000 sites. The workflow integrates spatial data, administrative boundaries, a digital elevation model, and protected-area data to characterize the distribution of wind energy infrastructure.

2. Packages

library(sf)
## Linking to GEOS 3.9.3, GDAL 3.5.2, PROJ 8.2.1; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
library(dplyr)
##

library(ggplot2)
library(terra)
## terra 1.7.71
library(leaflet)
library(geodata)

3. Data Upload and Inspection

The datasets were uploaded to the R environment and inspected before analysis

load("data/adm0_pt.rda")
names(adm0_pt)
## [1] "geom"
load("data/adm1_pt.rda")
names(adm1_pt)
## [1] "Distrito" "geom"
load("data/rn2000.rda")
names(rn2000)
## [1] "SITE_CODE" "SITE_NAME" "AREA__HA_" "TIPO"      "geometry"
load("data/e2p.rda")
names(e2p)
## [1] "nome"                            "tecnologia"                     
## [3] "distrito_regiao_autonoma"        "latitude_wgs84_o"               
## [5] "longitude_wgs84_o"               "potencia_instalada_mw"          
## [7] "estado"                          "ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento"

4. Wind Facilities as Spatial Points

Longitude and latitude coordinates were converted to numeric values and used to create point geometries in WGS84 (EPSG:4326)

e2p$longitude_wgs84_o <- as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", e2p$longitude_wgs84_o))
e2p$latitude_wgs84_o <- as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", e2p$latitude_wgs84_o))

e2p_sf <- st_as_sf(e2p,
  coords = c("longitude_wgs84_o",
    "latitude_wgs84_o"), crs = 4326)

5. CRS Standardization

All spatial datasets were standardized to WGS84 (EPSG:4326)

adm0_pt <- st_transform(adm0_pt, 4326)
adm1_pt <- st_transform(adm1_pt, 4326)
rn2000 <- st_transform(rn2000, 4326)

6. Geometry Cleaning

Empty geometries were removed and invalid geometries were corrected

e2p_sf <- e2p_sf[!st_is_empty(e2p_sf), ]

adm0_pt <- st_make_valid(adm0_pt)
adm1_pt <- st_make_valid(adm1_pt)
rn2000 <- st_make_valid(rn2000)

Question 1. Map the wind energy facilities in mainland Portugal regarding the country and district borders. Apply the appropriate legend and choose one aggregation level (legend) to wind energy facilities.

7. Facilities in Mainland Portugal

Only facilities located within mainland Portugal were retained

e2p_pt <- st_filter(e2p_sf,adm0_pt)

8. Installed Capacity by District

Installed capacity was converted from character to numeric format

e2p_sf$potencia_instalada_mw <- as.numeric(gsub(",", ".", e2p_sf$potencia_instalada_mw))

e2p_pt <- st_filter(e2p_sf, adm0_pt)

e2p_district <- st_join(e2p_pt,adm1_pt,join = st_within)

The installed capacity and number of facilities were then aggregated by administrative district

district_summary <- e2p_district %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(Distrito) %>%
  summarise(n_facilities = n(),
    total_capacity_mw = sum(potencia_instalada_mw,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop")

adm1_map <- adm1_pt %>%
  left_join(district_summary,by = "Distrito")

Installed Capacity by District

map_facilities <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = adm1_map,
    aes(fill = total_capacity_mw),
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = e2p_pt,
    aes(size = potencia_instalada_mw),
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_sf(data = adm0_pt,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c(
      "#9dd5a4",
      "#78b87c",
      "#5ea059",
      "#48843e",
      "#396a29",
      "#2a4f19"),
    name = "Installed capacity (MW)",
    na.value = "grey90") +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Facility capacity (MW)") +
  labs(title = "Wind energy facilities in mainland Portugal",
    subtitle = "Installed capacity aggregated by district",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

print(map_facilities)

Figure 1: Map of the spatial distribution of wind energy facilities in mainland Portugal in relation to national and district boundaries. The map illustrates the geographic distribution and density of wind farms across districts.

Question 2. Map the wind facilities and its distribution regarding elevation and protected areas. Find the the appropriate theme for the digital elevation model.

9. Digital Elevation Model

A 30 arc-second SRTM-derived digital elevation model was obtained using the geodata package and cropped to mainland Portugal.

dem <- elevation_30s(country = "PRT",path = "data")

dem <- crop(dem,vect(adm0_pt))

dem <- mask(dem,vect(adm0_pt))

DEM Visualization

plot(dem,  col = terrain.colors(50),
  main = "Digital Elevation Model - Mainland Portugal")

10. Elevation at Wind Facilities

Elevation values were extracted from the DEM at each wind facility

e2p_pt$elevation_m <- terra::extract(dem, vect(e2p_pt))[, 2]

Wind Facilities and Elevation

plot(dem,  col = terrain.colors(50),
  main = "Wind energy facilities, elevation and Natura 2000")

plot(vect(rn2000),
  add = TRUE,
  border = "brown",
  col = NA,
  lwd = 0.8)

plot(vect(e2p_pt),
  add = TRUE,
  pch = 20,
  col = "black")

plot(vect(adm0_pt),
  add = TRUE,
  border = "black",
  lwd = 2)

Figure 2: Spatial overlay of wind energy facilities with topography (Digital Elevation Model) and protected areas within the Natura 2000 Network. The map highlights the intersection of 70 wind energy facilities with 13 distinct Natura 2000 sites across 11 mainland districts.

Question 3. How are facilities distributed in relation to altitude? plot the attitudinal distribution and describe

11. Altitudinal Distribution

The altitudinal distribution of wind energy facilities was evaluated using a histogram and descriptive statistics.

elevation_plot <- ggplot(st_drop_geometry(e2p_pt),
  aes(x = elevation_m)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30,
    fill = "#00a600",
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(e2p_pt$elevation_m,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    color = "#B2182B") +
  annotate("text",
    x = median(e2p_pt$elevation_m,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    y = Inf,
    label = paste0("Median = ",
      round(median(e2p_pt$elevation_m,
          na.rm = TRUE),1)," m"),
    vjust = 1.5,
    hjust = -0.05,
    size = 4) +
  labs(title = "Altitudinal distribution of wind energy facilities",
    subtitle = "Elevation at facility locations across mainland Portugal",
    x = "Elevation (m)",
    y = "Number of facilities") +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 15),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "grey35"),
    axis.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 15, 10, 10))

print(elevation_plot)
## Warning: Removed 4 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range
## (`stat_bin()`).

Figure 3. Elevational distribution of wind energy facilities in mainland Portugal.

Wind energy facilities were distributed across a broad altitudinal range, from 29 to 1,340 m. The median elevation was 855 m, while the mean was 719 m. Half of the facilities were located between 322 and 1,034 m. The higher median than means suggests an asymmetric distribution, with a concentration of facilities at relatively high elevations and a smaller number occurring at lower elevations.

Descriptive Statistics

elevation_summary <- e2p_pt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    minimum = min(elevation_m, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = quantile(elevation_m, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(elevation_m, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(elevation_m, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q3 = quantile(elevation_m, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum = max(elevation_m, na.rm = TRUE)
)

elevation_summary

Question 4. What was the total national installed capacity (in GW) in 2019?

12. Total Installed Capacity in 2019

The total installed wind energy capacity up to 2019 was calculated

capacity_2019 <- e2p_pt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento <= 2019) %>%
  summarise(total_MW = sum(potencia_instalada_mw,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    total_GW = total_MW / 1000)

capacity_2019
## # A tibble: 1 × 2
##   total_MW total_GW
##      <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1    5367.     5.37

The total national installed wind energy capacity in mainland Portugal in 2019 was approximately 5.37 GW.

Question 5. How has it grown (installed GW) since the first installed facility?

13. Growth of Installed Capacity

Annual and cumulative installed capacity were calculated according to the commissioning year of each facility

capacity_growth <- e2p_pt %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(
    ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento) %>%
  summarise(
    annual_MW = sum(potencia_instalada_mw,na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento) %>%
  mutate(cumulative_GW = cumsum(annual_MW) / 1000)

capacity_growth
## # A tibble: 24 × 3
##    ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento annual_MW cumulative_GW
##    <chr>                               <dbl>         <dbl>

##  2 1996                                 10.2        0.012 
##  3 1998                                 31.2        0.0432
##  4 1999                                 11.7        0.0549
##  5 2000                                 46.1        0.101 
##  6 2001                                 40.4        0.141 
##  7 2002                                 94.2        0.236 
##  8 2003                                102.         0.337 
##  9 2004                                335.         0.672 
## 10 2005                                592.         1.26  
## # ℹ 14 more rows

Growth Plot

growth_plot <- ggplot(capacity_growth,
  aes(x = ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento,
    y = cumulative_GW)
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Growth of installed wind energy capacity",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Cumulative installed capacity (GW)") +
  theme_minimal()

growth_plot
## `geom_line()`: Each group consists of only one observation.
## ℹ Do you need to adjust the group aesthetic?

Figure 4. Temporal growth of cumulative installed wind energy capacity in mainland Portugal. The cumulative installed capacity reflects the progressive addition of wind energy facilities according to their commissioning year, expressed in gigawatts (GW).

14. Wind Facilities and Natura 2000

Wind facilities were spatially intersected with Natura 2000 sites

e2p_natura <- st_join(e2p_pt,
  rn2000,
  join = st_intersects,
  left = FALSE)

n_facilities_natura <- nrow(e2p_natura)

n_facilities_natura
## [1] 70

15. Natura 2000 Sites Intersected

Distinct Natura 2000 sites intersected by wind facilities were identified

intersected_sites <- e2p_natura %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(
    SITE_CODE,
    SITE_NAME,
    TIPO)

natura_sites_intersected <- nrow(intersected_sites)

intersected_sites

Question 6. Are protected areas affected? Where and to which extent (number of Sites)?

16. Natura 2000 by District

The number of intersecting facilities and Natura 2000 sites was summarized by district

natura_district <- st_join(e2p_natura,
  adm1_pt,
  join = st_within)

natura_by_district <- natura_district %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(Distrito) %>%
  summarise(intersected_facilities = n(),
    intersected_sites = n_distinct(SITE_CODE),
    .groups = "drop")

17. Wind Facilities and Natura 2000 Map

map_natura <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = rn2000,
    fill = "grey80",
    color = NA,
    alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_sf(data = adm1_pt,
    fill = NA,
    color = "white",
    linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = e2p_pt,
    color = "black",
    size = 1) +
  geom_sf(data = e2p_natura,
    color = "red",
    size = 2) +
  geom_sf(data = adm0_pt,
    fill = NA,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(title = "Wind facilities and Natura 2000 sites",
    subtitle = "Facilities intersecting Natura 2000 sites are highlighted",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

map_natura

Figure 5. Spatial distribution of wind energy facilities and Natura 2000 sites in mainland Portugal. Natura 2000 sites are shown in grey, while wind energy facilities are represented by black points. Facilities intersecting Natura 2000 sites are highlighted in red.

A total of 70 wind energy facilities intersect Natura 2000 protected areas, encompassing 13 distinct Natura 2000 sites across 11 mainland Portuguese districts. Viseu had the highest number of facilities intersecting protected areas (25), followed by Vila Real (13) and Leiria (7).

18. CHALLENGE: Interactive Map

An interactive map was created to allow inspection of individual wind facilities and their main attributes.

e2p_leaflet <- st_transform(e2p_pt,4326)

# Creating an interactive map of wind energy facilities
interactive_map <- leaflet(e2p_leaflet) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(radius = 5,
    stroke = TRUE,
    fillOpacity = 0.8,
    popup = ~paste0("<b>Facility:</b> ",
      nome,"<br><b>Commissioning year:</b> ",
      ano_de_entrada_em_funcionamento,
      "<br><b>Installed capacity:</b> ",
      potencia_instalada_mw," MW"))

interactive_map

Figure 6. Interactive map of wind energy facilities in mainland Portugal. Each point represents an individual wind facility, with pop-up information providing its name, commissioning year, and installed capacity.
